text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. Most APIs communicate over HTTP requests, where you send a request to a server and receive data in return. This data is usually formatted as JSON, a lightweight and readable structure that is easy to parse in almost any programming language. Before you can access an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, because networks fail and servers return unexpected responses.
